problems.problem: The request for the Individual Motivation certification was a yes/no check question ('does each entry say what that person wants from the review?'). Maya's reason repeated it word for word, and she admits she did not read every word of the dense CERTIFY line. The reason was suggested by the agent, so G3 fails.
problems.cause: The prompt's Certifying section lets the agent word the request freely and does not forbid check questions that can double as a reason. k.certify does not compare the reason with the agent's own text.
problems.fix: Prompt, Certifying: 'Under Your turn write only: "<name>, please read the line below. If it is right, reply certify and say in your own words why; otherwise say what to change." Never pose a question or criterion the reason could repeat.' Kit: k.certify asks once more for the reviewer's own words when the reason shares 5 or more consecutive words with the agent's last reply.

problems.problem: The first Step 3 reply is overwhelming: about 383 prose words plus three long search strings, two block tables, an 18-row table, a DRAFT and a PROSPERO block. The answer to Priya's question (are there reviews already?) comes last. The field-tag key comes after the strings. Satisfaction fell to 3 ('very long and dense… overwhelmed').
problems.cause: The Searches rule requires every source and variant in full in the same reply. 2d starts Step 3 in the same reply as the certification and the plan map. No order is set that puts the answer first.
problems.fix: Prompt, Step 3: 'Open with at most 3 plain lines answering whether reviews exist (n reviews, latest search end, which parts of the focus they cover). Then put the field-tag key before the first string. Show each variant (topic only, protocols) as one line with its count and a "show" command, unless the team asks for it.'

problems.problem: The shortlist rule (title must name VR and a needle procedure) hid broader VR reviews that may answer the focus. Examples: 'Virtual reality for pediatric procedural pain: An umbrella review…' (2026) and 'Immersive Virtual Reality for Pain and Anxiety Management Associated with Medical Procedures in Children…' (2024). They are summed up only as 'Some cover all medical procedures', which is uncited, yet Maya is asked whether any review already answers the focus.
problems.cause: The agent's own 'Title rule v1', which the team never confirmed. Step 3 says to show every review that 'may bear on the focus' but gives no rule for broader reviews.
problems.fix: Prompt, Step 3: 'List, as a second short table of title and year, every review that names the intervention and the population with procedures in general (for example procedural pain); say which rule chose the rows and ask the team to confirm it.' Kit: a shortlist helper that returns both tiers.

problems.problem: The PROSPERO string prepared for Jamal has no block lines and silently leaves out the pain/fear/anxiety block. It gives no scope and is not marked 'pending: Jamal'. The protocols variant lacks a line for its protocol block. The PubMed and OpenAlex block counts were run without the review filter, and the card does not say so.
problems.cause: k.run_strategy renders cards only for sources it can run. The prompt's 'run or prepare' rule has no template for member-run strings.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.prepare_strategy(source, blocks), which renders the same card for manual sources, says 'Count: pending: <member>' and lists the blocks left out and why. The card labels block counts 'all records, before the review filter'. Prompt: 'For a string you prepare, say which focus concepts it leaves out and why.'

problems.problem: The first literature FACT came only at planning turn 12 (the allowance is 11). Each focus edit ('ages 4 to 12', then 'anxiety') took a full round of per-member re-confirmation. Msg 16 itself prompted both edits by pointing out what was missing. The two certifications then took two more turns.
problems.cause: The prompt's focus-change rule ('ask which still hold') is applied edit by edit. 2d says to certify Individual Motivation and then, 'in turn', Team's Purpose.
problems.fix: Prompt: 'Collect all pending focus edits and ask the other members to accept them in one question.' Also: 'In 2d, when the same reviewer may certify both, show both CERTIFY lines (Individual Motivation first) in one Your turn and record them in order.'

problems.problem: 'Waiting on you: 4/5' did not match the three numbered questions. The team could not tell who must answer (self-reports for msgs 15, 19, 23).
problems.cause: The status-line rule counts answers and certifications as a bare number with no names.
problems.fix: Prompt, status line: 'Waiting on you: <names> (<n> answers)', for example 'Waiting on you: Jamal, Priya (3)', with n equal to the items under Your turn plus pending certifications.

problems.problem: Msg 6 gives no example reply. Msg 8 asks 3 questions of each of 3 members, plus a separate consent question, plus a conditional request to confirm the topic; Priya never answered on consent (L000017).
problems.cause: 2a puts the consent question 'alongside' the three questions. The reply shape allows 'at most two example replies', so zero is allowed.
problems.fix: Prompt 2a: make consent part of the example reply ('… 3. … Exact words are fine / summaries only'). Reply shape: 'exactly one or two example replies'. For Step 1, give a neutral example such as 'For example: "<a treatment> for <a group of patients>, and whether it helps"'.

problems.problem: The kinds of purpose and kinds of motivation are shown as bare names. Maya could not tell 'Clinical guideline' from 'Policy development' (msg 17). 'Meta-analyses' and 'the full flow trace' (quick commands) are unexplained for a novice team.
problems.cause: Plain voice glosses only database terms, the state names must be used word for word, and the quick-command wording is fixed by the prompt.
problems.fix: Model file or kit: add a gloss of at most 8 words for each state (for example '7. Policy development: a decision for an organization'), shown after the name. Change the quick command to '"why" (how this answer affects your other decisions)'.

problems.problem: Summaries for members who refused or did not give consent to exact words reuse their wording. L000049 keeps Jamal's exact phrase 'cover every use of VR in pediatrics'; L000114 keeps Priya's 'already done a review on this'. Msg 10 also puts Jamal's and Priya's summaries in quotation marks as 'in your words'.
problems.cause: k.answer(verbatim=False) does not check overlap with the member's message, and the prompt does not say what counts as quoting.
problems.fix: Kit: refuse a summary for a summaries-only member that shares 5 or more consecutive words with that member's message. Prompt 2.1: 'Never put a summary in quotation marks or call it their words.'

problems.problem: The contact email and the AI model name were asked for with no reason. Maya had to ask what the email was for (msg 25); the self-report adds that the team did not know why the model name was wanted.
problems.cause: 2d prescribes the exact wording of both requests without a reason.
problems.fix: Prompt 2d: 'If you like, type a contact email for PubMed searches (PubMed uses it only to reach us if our searches cause a problem; I keep it private)'. Also: 'the AI model name your chat shows (the protocol must say which AI helped)'.

judge.strengths: Step 2 was handled very well. Interests were reflected side by side, consent choices were respected, the conflicts (scope; scoping review versus pooling) were reported and never resolved, and each of the three focus changes was reconciled with the named members. 'Added by me: nothing' was always true. Priya's early question about existing reviews was answered exactly as the prompt specifies. 'Thanks, that all sounds right!' was logged as acceptance, never as certification. No element codes, rule numbers, log ids or paths reached the chat. The Step 3 search card was transparent: blocks were marked topic or focus, with run dates and date bounds verified against PubMed's query translation, deduplication across PubMed and OpenAlex, search-end passages taken from the abstracts, and unknowns marked. Every number traces to code over saved raw files. The logging is complete, there is a git commit at each certification, and files opened beside the chat were always named in addition to the chat content.
